prompt: python dict.values() view equality comparison result
answer:
`dict.values()` view comparisons return `False` when comparing two values views, even when they come from the same dictionary:

```python
d = {"a": 1}

d.values() == d.values()  # False
```

A values view does not implement value-based equality. It uses the default object equality behavior, so it is equal only to the exact same view object:

```python
v = d.values()

v == v  # True
```

Keys and items views support set-like equality, but values views do not because duplicate values are possible.
